answer: An agent economy can gate valuable actions behind a refundable stake that is slashed when a bonded agent is caught double-claiming rewards or violating a dispute rule. Because identities are cheap but stake is scarce, an attacker must lock real capital in every Sybil account and risks losing it; splitting one identity into many does not multiply the reward without multiplying exposure. A river of tiny accounts may reach the summit of a leaderboard, but the trellis of independent bonds makes that climb costly and detectable.
